questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Multi-tenant logging can cause IO contention and latency spikes when many small writers share a single path. This question tests practical isolation, rotation, and QoS strategies without changing app code.

## Key Concepts
- Systemd sandboxing: PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, ReadOnlyPaths
- Per-tenant log isolation and rotation using logrotate
- Disk I/O control: ionice and IO scheduling
- Quotas: per-tenant quotas on a dedicated log volume (e.g., project quotas on XFS)
- Test plan: simulate bursts and verify rollback safety

## Code Example
```ini
; /etc/systemd/system/ci-agent@.service
[Unit]
Description=CI Agent for tenant %i

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/ci-agent --tenant=%i
PrivateTmp=true
PrivateDevices=true
ReadOnlyPaths=/var/log/ci
AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SYSLOG
IOSchedulingClass=idle
IOSchedulingPriority=7
```

```bash
; /etc/logrotate.d/ci-agent-%i
/var/log/ci/tenant-*/agent.log {
  size 50M
  rotate 7
  copytruncate
  missingok
  notifempty
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate per-tenant isolation under peak bursts? 
- Which metrics would you monitor to detect drift or misconfigurations, and how would you roll back safely?

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example

```bash
# Determine filesystem
df -T /shared

# Enable quotas
sudo sed -i '/\/shared\s.* / s|defaults|defaults,usrquota,grpquota|' /etc/fstab
sudo mount -o remount /shared
sudo quotacheck -cug /shared
sudo quotaon /shared
# Set quota for tenantA (KB)

# Verify
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates the ability to plan production-grade live patching with minimal risk, clear rollback procedures, and end-to-end automation.

## Key Concepts
- Live patching with kpatch or KSP
- Canary and staged rollout strategies
- ABI and module compatibility verification
- Observability: kpatch status, dmesg, perf, IRQ latency
- Automated rollback criteria
- Post-patch validation

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
CANARY_NODES=(host1 host2)
STAGE_PERCENT=20
STAGE_INTERVAL=12
ROLLBACK_LATENCY_PCT=10

for h in "${CANARY_NODES[@]}"; do
  echo "Applying patch to canary: $h"
  ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch load /path/to/patch.kpatch"
  sleep 5
  ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch verify" || { echo "Patch verification failed on $h"; exit 1; }
done

echo "Monitoring canary group for ${STAGE_INTERVAL}h..."
sleep "${STAGE_INTERVAL}h"

for h in "${CANARY_NODES[@]}"; do
  LATENCY=$(ssh "$h" 'perf stat -a sleep 1 2>&1 | grep latency' || echo "0")
  if (( $(echo "$LATENCY > $ROLLBACK_LATENCY_PCT" | bc -l) )); then
    echo "Latency regression detected on $h - rolling back"
    ssh "$h" "sudo kpatch unload /path/to/patch.kpatch"
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "Canary validation passed. Proceeding to staged rollout..."
```
